open_questions: Period coincides with stellar rotation to within 0.2% with large spot modulation amplitude exceeding transit depth, leaving spot-generated or tidally locked binary degeneracy unresolved
Gaia FLAME/GSP-Phot radius 0.712-0.709 vs TIC 0.61 gives duration_ratio 1.16-1.17 vs 1.36 and increases planet size to 4.47-4.49 Rearth, near inflated hot Jupiter range
Significant transit-to-transit depth scatter (p_consistent 1.3289317435047993e-14) and one 8816 ppm outlier at btjd 1934.617 - needs detrending checks but mean SNR 24.95 over 23 transits remains high
dossier.public_summary: A steady 3.8 Earth-radius dip repeats cleanly every 1.36 days on the target star with no odd-even difference or secondary eclipse and a flat-bottomed shape. The star's own spot cycle has almost the same period and larger variability, so a spotted star or stellar binary could mimic the signal without radial velocities, but size and on-target location make a planet the best explanation for now.

reasons.why: Undiluted radius is well below the planet / brown-dwarf boundary and inconsistent with a stellar eclipse on the target, despite density tension.
Difference imaging puts the dip on the target (offset 3.162 arcsec +/-1.999 sigma 1.582) and rules out all neighbours that could cause it (closest suspects 46.7 sigma from centroid away).
Transit shape is not V-shaped (V test 0.9161), consistent with a planetary transit, high impact parameter (fit_b 0.8258) explaining long observed duration.
No significant secondary at phase 0.6242 or at half phase and no odd/even depth difference, disfavouring an eclipsing binary at 1.36 d or 2.72 d.
reasons.value: secondary snr 1.72 (depth_ppm 221.2) and best_brightening_snr 13.46, odd_even diff_sigma 1.86

reasons.why: Star rotates at 1.361 d with amplitude 15792 ppm vs 16951 ppm, indistinguishable from the 1.36 d transit period; signal_period_d 1.36484 is 1-1 multiple, so coincidence and large phase_curve amplitude 2719 ppm cannot be separated from parent-binary light without RV, but size, centroid and non-V shape positively favour planet over binary.
